safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not state the patient is haemodynamically stable.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: In suspected acute coronary syndrome, documenting haemodynamic stability helps convey immediate acuity and supports appropriate triage/urgency for EMS and receiving teams. Omission may reduce clarity of the patient’s current risk status but is unlikely to directly change the decision to send an ambulance in this scenario.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient was examined while seated at rest.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not state patient was examined seated at rest.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Whether the patient was assessed seated at rest provides context for symptom severity and any observed distress, which can inform urgency and interpretation of reported dyspnoea/chest pressure. Its omission mainly reduces assessment quality/continuity rather than directly driving a specific treatment error.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient appears well perfused on video inspection.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not mention appearing well perfused on video inspection.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not recording that the patient appeared well perfused removes an important remote “general appearance” datapoint relevant to shock/poor circulation in a chest-pain emergency. This is primarily a loss of clinical context that could affect perceived severity but is less likely to cause direct harm if EMS dispatch is already underway.

safety_verdicts.content: Urgent ECG and troponin T are required.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated mentions ECG but does not include troponin T requirement.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the need for troponin testing (along with ECG) in a possible MI can contribute to incomplete or delayed diagnostic workup and risk stratification if subsequent clinicians rely on the note. In ACS, delayed biomarker testing can delay confirmation and escalation of care.

This can plausibly affect safety and treatment decisions during handover to EMS/ED.
